\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{باردار} (bârdâr)}{باردار (bârdâr)}]{\fa{باردار} (bârdâr) — pregnant}

\label{lesson:FA-C332-bardar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to evacuate, then the Persian for to take shelter.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{باردار}}
\textbf{\fa{باردار}} (\emph{bârdâr}) — \textquotedblleft{}pregnant\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{خواهرم} \fa{پنج} \fa{ماه} \fa{است} \fa{که} \fa{باردار} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Khâharam panj mâh ast ke bârdâr ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My sister has been pregnant for five months.
\end{quote}

\emph{bâr} \textquotedblleft{}load\textquotedblright{} + \emph{dâr} \textquotedblleft{}having\textquotedblright{}. \emph{Hâmele} is a synonym of Arabic origin.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{bârdâr} joins \emph{bâr} \textquotedblleft{}load, burden\textquotedblright{} and \emph{dâr-}, the present stem of \emph{dâshtan} \textquotedblleft{}to have, to hold\textquotedblright{}: carrying a load. Both parts are native Persian; EtymDB lists no entry.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bârdâr}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bârdâr}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{bârdâr}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to evacuate, then the Persian for to take shelter, then say \emph{bârdâr} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{باردار} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Pregnant\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{زایمان} (zâymân)}{زایمان (zâymân)}]{\fa{زایمان} (zâymân) — childbirth, a delivery}

\label{lesson:FA-C332-zayman}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to take shelter, then the Persian for pregnant.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{زایمان}}
\textbf{\fa{زایمان}} (\emph{zâymân}) — \textquotedblleft{}childbirth, a delivery\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{زایمان} \fa{او} \fa{در} \fa{بیمارستان} \fa{خوب} \fa{پیش} \fa{رفت}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Zâymân-e u dar bimârestân khub pish raft.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Her delivery at the hospital went well.
\end{quote}

From \emph{zâ-}, the present stem of \emph{zâyidan} \textquotedblleft{}to give birth\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{zâymân} is built on \emph{zâ-}, the present stem of the native verb \emph{zâyidan} \textquotedblleft{}to give birth\textquotedblright{}, with the noun suffix \emph{-mân}. EtymDB lists no entry.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{zâymân}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{zâymân}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{zâymân}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to take shelter, then the Persian for pregnant, then say \emph{zâymân} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{به} \fa{دنیا} \fa{آمدن} (be donyâ âmadan)}{به دنیا آمدن (be donyâ âmadan)}]{\fa{به} \fa{دنیا} \fa{آمدن} (be donyâ âmadan) — to be born}

\label{lesson:FA-C332-be-donya-amadan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for pregnant, then the Persian for childbirth.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{به} \fa{دنیا} \fa{آمدن}}
\textbf{\fa{به} \fa{دنیا} \fa{آمدن}} (\emph{be donyâ âmadan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to be born\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{پسرم} \fa{در} \fa{یک} \fa{شب} \fa{برفی} \fa{به} \fa{دنیا} \fa{آمد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Pesaram dar yek shab-e barfi be donyâ âmad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My son was born on a snowy night.
\end{quote}

Literally \textquotedblleft{}to come into the world\textquotedblright{}. \emph{Be donyâ âvardan} is \textquotedblleft{}to give birth to\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{donyâ} \textquotedblleft{}world\textquotedblright{} is borrowed from Arabic \emph{dunyā} (EtymDB). \emph{âmadan} \textquotedblleft{}to come\textquotedblright{} is inherited Persian; EtymDB takes it back to the Indo-European root \emph{g\textsuperscript{w}em-} \textquotedblleft{}to step\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{be donyâ âmadan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{be donyâ âmadan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{be donyâ âmadan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for pregnant, then the Persian for childbirth, then say \emph{be donyâ âmadan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{به} \fa{دنیا} \fa{آمدن} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To be born\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{نوزاد} (nowzâd)}{نوزاد (nowzâd)}]{\fa{نوزاد} (nowzâd) — a newborn baby}

\label{lesson:FA-C332-nowzad}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for childbirth, then the Persian for to be born.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{نوزاد}}
\textbf{\fa{نوزاد}} (\emph{nowzâd}) — \textquotedblleft{}a newborn baby\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{نوزاد} \fa{تمام} \fa{شب} \fa{گریه} \fa{میکرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Nowzâd tamâm-e shab gerye mikard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The newborn baby cried all night.
\end{quote}

\emph{now} \textquotedblleft{}new\textquotedblright{} + \emph{zâd} \textquotedblleft{}born\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{zâdan} \textquotedblleft{}to give birth\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{nowzâd} joins \emph{now} \textquotedblleft{}new\textquotedblright{} and \emph{zâd} \textquotedblleft{}born\textquotedblright{}, the past stem of \emph{zâdan} \textquotedblleft{}to give birth\textquotedblright{}. Both parts are native Persian; EtymDB lists no entry.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{تربیت} \fa{کردن} (tarbiyat kardan)}{تربیت کردن (tarbiyat kardan)}]{\fa{تربیت} \fa{کردن} (tarbiyat kardan) — to bring up, to raise (a child)}

\label{lesson:FA-C332-tarbiyat-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to be born, then the Persian for a newborn baby.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{تربیت} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{تربیت} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{tarbiyat kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to bring up, to raise (a child)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{مادربزرگم} \fa{شش} \fa{بچه} \fa{را} \fa{تربیت} \fa{کرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Mâdarbozorgam shesh bachche râ tarbiyat kard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My grandmother brought up six children.
\end{quote}

It stresses manners and education. Present \emph{tarbiyat mikonad}. \emph{Tarbiyat-e badani} is \textquotedblleft{}physical education\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{tarbiyat} is usually traced to Arabic \emph{tarbiya}, \textquotedblleft{}upbringing, education\textquotedblright{}; EtymDB lists no entry. \emph{kardan} \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{} is inherited Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tarbiyat kardan}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to be born, then the Persian for a newborn baby, then say \emph{tarbiyat kardan} again
\end{itemize}
